name: Rabat, Modern Capital and Historic City: a Shared Heritage
description: Rabat, Morocco's capital, sits on the Atlantic coast where the Bou Regreg river meets the sea. Two eras share the city: a 12th-century Almohad core of ramparts, gates and the unfinished Hassan Mosque, begun in 1184, and a vast planned new town from the French Protectorate, laid out with administrative quarters and the Jardins d'Essais gardens. Together they make one of Africa's most complete modern city plans.
